speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and how long have you had these symptoms? Additionally, have you noticed any itching, pain, or hair loss in the affected areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap). While the family history of psoriasis is noted, the age of onset, location (scalp/forehead), and description of red, scaly rash in a 3-month-old are classic for seborrheic dermatitis. I recommend a trial of gentle shampooing with ketoconazole; if there is no improvement or if the rash becomes thick and crusty, please return for a KOH preparation to rule out tinea capitis.
